site.name: Alessandro Luppi
site.title: Alessandro Luppi — Software and AI engineer
site.description: Alessandro Luppi builds full-stack software and AI-powered products, end to end. A short introduction, and a way to get in touch.

product.label: In the product
product.title: AI people actually use
product.body: Not a demo bolted to the side. AI built into features people rely on, and held to the same standard as everything around it.

practice.label: In the work
practice.title: A faster way to build
practice.body: Agents in the daily loop: planning, writing, reviewing. The judgement stays human. The typing mostly doesn't.

page.label: In front of you
page.title: This page, for instance
page.body: Designed, written and committed by an AI agent from a brief and a conversation, then reviewed line by line. You are looking at the output.

craft.label: Full-stack
craft.title: The same care, whatever the shape.
craft.body: From the data model to the last pixel — web, mobile, and whatever else the product needs to become.

contact.title: Let's talk.
contact.body: Ideas, problems, roles, or just something you're building. LinkedIn is the fastest way to reach me.

egg.title: One more thing.
egg.body: You made it to the bottom. Now try being the model that has to guess who I am.

footer.built: Built with Nuxt, written with an AI agent.

game.label: Easter egg
game.title: You are the model.
game.intro: Five sentences, each missing its last token. Pick what comes next. The percentages are what a naive predictor would guess — following them is exactly how a model gets a confident answer wrong. Whatever you pick also dresses the figure beside you.

job.reveal: Software engineer. Full-stack, which mostly means being the person who finds out why it broke in production.

hands.reveal: A keyboard — though a growing share of the typing now gets delegated to an agent.

head.reveal: Headphones. The only reliable way to make a compiler and an open-plan office coexist.

badge.prompt: If he wore a badge, it would read:
badge.reveal: Ships it. Quality is what survives contact with real users, not what looks good in a demo.

face.prompt: His face when the build passes first try:
face.reveal: Mild disbelief, followed immediately by checking whether the tests actually ran.

result.label: Inference complete
result.caption: Your prediction, assembled.
result.body: You just did what a model does: five guesses from a prior and a vibe. Which is roughly how this whole page got written — an agent predicting the next token, and a human deciding which predictions to keep.
